source: Schapiro et al. (2026) Measuring Combinatorial Creativity in LLMs and Humans (KOMBINE)
finding: First large blending benchmark for LLMs. Models are asked for a generic space plus a blended space for two random unrelated entities. Blending is the hardest of three tasks (association, analogy, blending).
numbers: 35 LLMs, temperature 0.9. Mean valid rate: association 59.0%, analogy 53.4%, blend 43.4%. Best model on blends 64.8% (gpt-5.6-sol), same model 55.4% on analogy.
limits: Judged by a panel of three LLMs; judges agree with humans 75% of the time only on items where the panel is unanimous. Entities sampled from Wikidata. Rubric requires a non-vacuous generic space, so scores depend on rubric strictness.
agent_relevance: Blending is the weakest open-mode operator for current models. Expect about half of raw blend attempts to fail the validity test; code must check validity and retry.

source: Schapiro et al. (2026) Measuring Combinatorial Creativity in LLMs and Humans (KOMBINE)
finding: The failure is in finding the generic space, not in building the blend. Given a valid shared abstraction, the blend itself is coherent.
numbers: Valid generic space found 43.4% of the time; given one, a coherent blended concept 97.1% of the time ('abstraction bottleneck'). Example: for Photosynthesis+Bread only Opus 4.6 found a valid generic space; other frontier models gave a bread-only schema.
limits: Every item was blended validly by at least one model, so no item was impossible. Explanation offered (lack of experiential knowledge) is a hypothesis, not tested.
agent_relevance: Split the blend operator into two steps: (1) find and verify a generic space that fits BOTH inputs, (2) project and elaborate. Put the check on step 1.

source: Schapiro et al. (2026) Measuring Combinatorial Creativity in LLMs and Humans (KOMBINE)
finding: LLM blends are homogeneous across models. Different models invent the same concept for the same pair, far more on blends than on analogies.
numbers: 2,070 invented concepts, 7,868 properties. 19.9% (412/2,070) share >=2 near-identical properties with another model's concept. Blends vs analogies: 94.7% vs 36.3% (>=1 shared property), 37.3% vs 2.6% (>=2); 14.3x. Same provider 2.3x more likely to coincide (9.3% vs 4.1%). DeepSeek +12.2pp, Anthropic +11.1pp, OpenAI -1.4pp vs baseline.
limits: Similarity threshold 0.674 (99th percentile of property-pair cosine). Embedding-based, so paraphrase matches count as repeats.
agent_relevance: Blends from one model, or from models of one family, are correlated (supports G4). Diversity must come from varying the input pair, not from resampling.

source: Schapiro et al. (2026) Measuring Combinatorial Creativity in LLMs and Humans (KOMBINE)
finding: Humans scored below nearly every LLM on all three tasks, mostly because humans less often produced a valid connection. Difficulty order differs: LLMs find association easier than analogy; humans find analogy easier.
numbers: 75 Prolific participants kept of 120 (screened for AI use), 5 items per task. Valid rates humans vs LLM mean: association 22.1% vs 59.0%, analogy 32.9% vs 53.4%, blend 12.8% vs 43.4%. Humans and LLMs also occupy different regions of semantic space.
limits: Online sample, 5 items each; skipped items scored zero, which lowers human scores. Not expert humans.
agent_relevance: Human-model complementarity: for diversity, a human or a different pool of sources may add what model resampling cannot.

source: Schapiro et al. (2026) Measuring Combinatorial Creativity in LLMs and Humans (KOMBINE)
finding: Scores across tasks are correlated; association originality predicts everything else. Leaders differ by task.
numbers: Association-analogy r=0.71, analogy-blending r=0.70, blending-association r=0.54 (all p<0.001). Association originality vs analogy originality r=0.73, vs blend originality r=0.42, vs valid blend r=0.48. claude-opus-4.6 led association and analogy; gpt-5.6-sol led blending.
limits: Correlation across 35 models, confounded by model size and release date.
agent_relevance: Model choice for the blend operator may differ from the main reasoner. Test per operator.

source: Schapiro et al. (2026) Measuring Combinatorial Creativity in LLMs and Humans (KOMBINE)
finding: The paper's blending prompt demands a form: one fused concept, triples tagged u / v / uv / emergent, at least one uv property that both inputs feed, plus emergent properties true of neither input. Vacuous schemas ('both exist') are rejected.
numbers: Prompt asks for exactly one blend, 4-6 triples. Judges score generic-space utility, coherence, and emergent structure.
limits: This is the benchmark's own prompt; no ablation of its parts is reported in the text I read.
agent_relevance: A ready-made template for the blend operator slot: uv-tagged shared property plus emergent property, checked by code for presence of both tags.

source: Wang et al. (2023) PopBlends: Strategies for Conceptual Blending with Large Language Models (CHI)
finding: A pipeline built on Fauconnier-Turner style blending: expand each input into associated traits/scenes, find connecting concepts, then merge scenes. GPT-3 or a knowledge-base method can do the expansion.
numbers: Annotation study: connecting concept related to both domains in 56.0% (No-GPT), 55.3% (Half-GPT), 58.7% (Full-GPT). At least one good concept among top five: 90.0%, 96.6%, 93.3%. Pooled 56.7% and 93.3%.
limits: GPT-3 (2021 era). Annotated by the authors. Pop-culture/product pairs only.
agent_relevance: One good output in five tries is near-certain: generate five connecting concepts, filter by code, keep the best.

source: Wang et al. (2023) PopBlends: Strategies for Conceptual Blending with Large Language Models (CHI)
finding: Quality of GPT-3 traits varied by type, and relatedness of generated scenes was higher for product than pop-culture scenes.
numbers: Trait accuracy: adjectives 79%, activities 58%, catchphrases 35%, all 57%. Scenes related to connecting concept: product 89.1%, pop culture 75.9% (raw 80.0% vs 63.4%); Stage 2 overall 98.3% related to own domain.
limits: Single annotator group; small set of domains (5 franchises, 6 products).
agent_relevance: Abstract, short traits (adjectives) are the reliable input to a blend; long specific recall (catchphrases) is not. Seed the generic space from abstract properties.

source: Wang et al. (2023) PopBlends: Strategies for Conceptual Blending with Large Language Models (CHI)
finding: User study: the system doubled the number of blend ideas people produced and reduced mental load.
numbers: 10 students, within-subject. Mean ideas per pair 2.03 (SD 0.84) vs 0.87 (SD 0.56) baseline search, Wilcoxon p<0.001. All 10 said PopBlends helped more. Abstract reports about half the mental demand (NASA-TLX).
limits: N=10, amateur designers, one session, pop-culture topic. Count of ideas, not independent quality rating.
agent_relevance: Scaffolded combine step increases idea count; supports a generate-many then filter loop for the open mode.

source: Ge and Parikh (2021) Visual Conceptual Blending with Large-scale Language and Vision Models
finding: Early LLM blending: ask a language model for the property linking two objects (reasoning), then render with CLIP-guided image models. Language models beat ConceptNet at proposing the linking property.
numbers: Simile dataset (Chakrabarty et al. 2020), 1000 candidates per method. P@10/P@100/P@1000: ConceptNet 0.13/7.69/37.33 vs best (largest GPT) 2.59/24.84/66.38 (row labels garbled in extraction, mapping approximate). Larger model gave higher precision. 96.34% of objects found in ConceptNet.
limits: Row labels partly lost in text extraction. Precision of one expected property, so many valid answers counted wrong. Only 20 blend descriptions in the image study.
agent_relevance: Pre-2022 evidence. Confirms model scale matters for the 'find the shared property' step; matches the 2026 finding that this step is the bottleneck.

source: Ge and Parikh (2021) Visual Conceptual Blending with Large-scale Language and Vision Models
finding: Image-side evaluation used six pairwise questions mapped to Fauconnier-Turner optimality principles (unpacking, integration, general quality).
numbers: 20 text descriptions of blends (half model-made, half human-made), AMT raters, three image models compared, six questions per pair.
limits: Counts and effect sizes were in a figure not recovered from text. Only a qualitative reading is safe.
agent_relevance: Evaluation criteria (recognise both inputs, integration, interest) can be turned into a code-checked rubric for a text blend.

source: Peng et al. (2025) Probing and Inducing Combinational Creativity in Vision-Language Models (IEI)
finding: Introduces Identification-Explanation-Implication (IEI): what was combined, how (shared attributes), and what it means. 666 artist-made visual mashups annotated this way. Best VLMs beat average humans on understanding but not experts.
numbers: Identification precision/recall: GPT-4o 75.67/85.00, Gemini-1.5-Pro 73.67/81.33, average human 53.42/70.33. Explanation precision: GPT-4o 74.19, Claude-3.5-Sonnet 74.19, average human 69.89. Implication win rate: human expert 78.3%, average human 51%, GPT-4o 73.5, GPT-4V 71.9, Gemini 71.7, Claude-3.5-Sonnet 62.9, Claude-3-Opus 39.2.
limits: Visual mashups only; 2024 models. Human baseline via Prolific. Replacement-type mashups were harder than fusion-type for humans. Table column mapping read from extracted text.
agent_relevance: Three-level decomposition is a testable form of generic-space work: name inputs, name shared attributes, then state the implication.

source: Peng et al. (2025) Probing and Inducing Combinational Creativity in Vision-Language Models (IEI)
finding: Generation: feeding the IEI structure (inputs, shared attributes, theme) into the prompt improved human-ranked creative quality over a version with only inputs and theme (II).
numbers: Friedman test across Human Expert / II / IEI, p<0.0001. Midjourney mean rank IEI 1.98 vs II 2.40; win rate vs expert 0.26 (II) to 0.35 (IEI). Prompt length did not differ (II 487.95 vs IEI 514.53, t=-0.84, p=0.404); in 46.0% of IEI wins the IEI prompt was shorter.
limits: Gain is smaller for weak image models (Stable Diffusion 3 minimal). Experts still ranked best.
agent_relevance: Evidence that an explicit shared-attributes step adds value beyond a longer prompt. Supports a mandatory generic-space slot.

source: Peng et al. (2025) Probing and Inducing Combinational Creativity in Vision-Language Models (IEI)
finding: Concept-level combination by the LLM is strong; execution is the bottleneck on the image side.
numbers: 90% (36 of 40) of DALLE-3 images made from GPT-4o descriptions integrated the objects and conveyed the theme; 27.8% (10 of 36) of well-crafted descriptions still failed to render well.
limits: Small sample, author judgement.
agent_relevance: For a text-only agent the execution gap is smaller; the concept step is the strong part when a generic space is supplied.

source: Gu et al. (2025) LLMs can Realize Combinatorial Creativity: Generating Creative Ideas via LLMs for Scientific Research
finding: An LLM agent loop that implements combination explicitly: store prior innovations at four abstraction levels (L1 domain-specific to L4 universal principle), retrieve analogues at each level by embedding, then recombine components into a new idea.
numbers: Claude-3.5-Sonnet backend, OAG-Bench papers. Similarity to the real follow-up paper: design rationale 0.85 vs 0.78 baseline, universal principle 0.83 vs 0.75, key mechanism 0.87 vs 0.77. Abstract: 7-10% gain.
limits: Success measure is embedding similarity (SPECTER) to what authors did, not novelty or usefulness. Baseline is a direct idea prompt only. Preprint; no human ratings.
agent_relevance: A working example of abstraction-level retrieval feeding a combine step. Level-by-level retrieval is a practical stand-in for a generic space.

source: Xu et al. (2026) Beyond Pixels: Visual Metaphor Transfer via Schema-Driven Agentic Reasoning
finding: Multi-agent system that operationalizes blending: perception agent writes a schema (subject, carrier, relational invariant = generic space, violation, emergent meaning); transfer agent keeps the invariant and picks a new carrier; generation agent writes the prompt; a diagnostic agent backtracks on failure.
numbers: Human study 100 participants, 45 images per method. Likert ratings full vs direct prompt: metaphor recognizability 4.47 vs 3.62, ingenuity 4.56 vs 2.75, violation appropriateness 4.51 vs 2.96, visual integration 4.74 vs 3.75, quality 4.76 vs 3.65. Preferred over GPT-Image 64.44%, Banana-pro 67.11%, Midjourney 72.89%, BAGEL 76.22% (GSB test, loser <10% vs the first two).
limits: System paper by the authors; LLM judges used in the automatic table. Visual task, not text reasoning.
agent_relevance: Same shape as the planned operator: extract invariant, re-instantiate in a new carrier, diagnose by level, retry.

source: Xu et al. (2026) Beyond Pixels: Visual Metaphor Transfer via Schema-Driven Agentic Reasoning
finding: Ablation separates scaffolding from prompt wording: a hand-written strong single prompt with full blending description helps, but the staged agent system still wins.
numbers: Human ratings (MR/MI/VA/VI/VQ): Direct 3.62/2.75/2.96/3.75/3.65; Strong prompt 3.97/3.69/3.77/3.89/4.09; w/o CBT description 3.88/3.66/3.68/4.04/4.12; w/o Transfer agent 4.01/3.71/3.83/4.33/4.25; w/o Diagnostic agent 4.26/4.05/3.98/4.61/4.48; Full 4.47/4.56/4.51/4.74/4.76. Alignment metric: +16.8% over runner-up.
limits: Authors' own ablation, one benchmark of 45 tasks.
agent_relevance: A single blending-template prompt gives most of the jump over a plain prompt; the diagnosis loop and transfer step add the rest. Try the cheap single pass first.

source: Song et al. (2025) Is a Peeled Apple Still Red? Conceptual Combination with Property Type (CCPT)
finding: Dataset of 12.3K noun-phrase / property / type triplets (component, emergent, canceled). LLMs can judge whether a property holds, but are poor at producing phrases with a required emergent property.
numbers: Judging: GPT-4o 95.6% accurate on 'has property', 69.6% on 'lacks property'; property-type labelling 56.4% vs human 81%. Noun-phrase completion emergent score E: GPT-4o base 23.1, human 38.0, gold 59.9.
limits: Table rows were ambiguous in the extracted text; only GPT-4o, human and gold values are quoted. LLM-as-judge metric validated against human judgement.
agent_relevance: Emergent properties are the product of a blend; models detect them better than they create them. Generate, then check that the property is true of the combo and of neither part.

source: Song et al. (2025) Is a Peeled Apple Still Red? Conceptual Combination with Property Type (CCPT)
finding: A spreading-activation prompt scaffold (iteratively expand related concepts from both parts using an LLM and ConceptNet, then combine) improved every generative task. Chain-of-thought alone barely changed emergence.
numbers: GPT-4o emergent property induction E: base 42.4, CoT 43.8, S.A. with LLM 45.8, S.A. with LLM+ConceptNet 57.8 (gold 58.4). Noun-phrase completion E: base 23.1, CoT 25.5, S.A. with both 38.9. Llama-3.1-70B emergent induction: base 42.5 to 54.6.
limits: Needs ConceptNet plus LLM expansion; many calls. Human check on N=30 sub-sample.
agent_relevance: A tested expansion step before combining gave +15 points where CoT gave about +1. Supports an 'expand both inputs' sub-step in the blend operator.

source: Sato (2025) The Way We Prompt: Conceptual Blending, Neural Dynamics, and Prompt-Induced Transitions in LLMs
finding: Blending-inspired prompt essay on LLMs (prompt-induced transitions and hallucinations). Largely conceptual and anecdotal.
numbers: No effect sizes or sample sizes found in the text I read; only a claim that effects repeat across models and sessions.
limits: Single author, no controls, no statistics reported. Treat as hypothesis only.
agent_relevance: None for design; do not cite as evidence that LLMs blend.

source: Sato (2025) Waking Up an AI: A Quantitative Framework for Prompt-Induced Phase Transition in LLMs
finding: Negative result for human-like blending. Prompts that fuse two distant concepts (aperiodic tilings plus traditional crafts) did not raise LLM engagement more than the same two themes presented side by side.
numbers: GPT-4o n=15 TQP evaluations and Gemini 2.5 Pro n=5; fused (TIPe) and non-fused (TIPn-e) both beat control (p<0.05 or 0.01) but fused vs non-fused showed no significant difference (one-tailed Welch t-test).
limits: Outcome is affective tone scored by another LLM; tiny n; not a test of blend quality. Models could describe the fusion-vs-separation contrast when asked.
agent_relevance: Warns that putting two concepts in one prompt is not integration. Integration must be checked by structure, not by tone or length.

source: Lu et al. (2025) Misty: UI Prototyping Through Interactive Conceptual Blending (CHI)
finding: An LLM-powered UI tool where a developer blends an example UI's parts into a work-in-progress UI. Users valued serendipitous blends but outputs often needed rework.
numbers: 14 front-end developers. 103 blending operations: global blending 36 (34.95%), drag-and-drop 35 (33.98%), regenerate 19 (18.5%). Mean satisfaction per blend 3.2 of 5 (median 3, SD 1.3); 28 of 103 rated neutral.
limits: Exploratory first-use study, no control condition. Satisfaction self-reported.
agent_relevance: Real LLM blend operations are mediocre on average (3.2/5): good as an idea source, not as a final answer. Pair with a check.

source: Matsuhira et al. (2024) Investigating Conceptual Blending of a Diffusion Model for Nonword-to-Image Generation (ACM MM)
finding: Blending can arise in a generative model with no blending training: interpolating two concept embeddings often yields images depicting both concepts.
numbers: Midpoint (ratio 0.5) of two prompts in Stable Diffusion: blended-concept depiction 0.621, mixed-concept depiction 0.862. Averaged over all ratios: 0.389 and 0.471. Peak at the midpoint.
limits: Image blending in embedding space, not semantic reasoning. Detected by automatic metrics.
agent_relevance: Blends can come from simple averaging in representation space, so the critique 'simpler process explains blends' applies. Compare structured blending against a plain averaging baseline.

source: Sun et al. (2025) Creative Blends of Visual Concepts
finding: AI design tool: LLM plus commonsense knowledge base maps an abstract concept to concrete objects through metaphor, then blends objects by shared attributes. User study: usability higher than baseline; abstract reports lower cognitive load and richer metaphor.
numbers: N=24 within-subject. Usability: t(23)=-2.547, p=0.018, Cohen's d=0.800 (large).
limits: Baseline is a standard image-generation workflow; novelty rated by participants.
agent_relevance: Shared-attribute matching used as the rule for which objects can be combined; attribute similarity is codeable.

source: Veale, O'Donoghue and Keane: Computation and Blending (Sapper model)
finding: Older AI system for conceptual integration. Sapper builds blends by spreading activation over a semantic network and finding shared structure. Authors argue the theory is tractable, because unchecked marker passing can become intractable.
numbers: No empirical numbers; a computational argument. Notes that unchecked spreading activation may visit most nodes of a connected network.
limits: Year and venue approximate (circa 2000); URL is the group page, not the paper. Toy knowledge bases.
agent_relevance: Classical precedent: spreading activation to find shared structure, with limits on search breadth. Matches the CCPT result that activation expansion helps.

source: Xi, Cheng, Soni and Turner (2026) poster on evaluating generative AI by conceptual integration (ACL 2026 workshop)
finding: Position poster arguing that creativity evaluation should measure conceptual integration, not only novelty. Seen as a search snippet only.
numbers: No numbers seen.
limits: Not opened; poster, proposal only.
agent_relevance: A possible rubric source; do not rely on it until read.
